items.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: someone like Mick Jagger would be sitting in a dark corner with glasses on trying to be as inconspicuous as possible, just kind of listening to the band.

ctx.x: Did people in the band ever go “what is he doing?” Well I mean you just basically said it, talking about the sax players, but did you ever say like oh my God, now he’s got this guy in here.

Well Gil was an institution, I mean before I met him. He led the band, his concept was he wants to see where the music can go. That is the whole thing, that sums it up. Some nights the band was pretty loose and some nights it was great. If we had a bad night everybody knew it, it happened. When the band was really on, the impact was incredible. It could happen for a lot of reasons, but sometimes just playing the arrangements themselves sometimes a couple of guys in the band would really be up and would have a…

played. If you played something jive you’d hear about it the next week. “Don’t do that anymore. Don’t do that.” But it was typical. We’d be playing some late night set at Sweet Basil’s on a Monday night and someone like Mick Jagger would be sitting in a dark corner with glasses on trying to be as inconspicuous as possible, just kind of listening to the band. Wow. And just a bunch of New York guys playing jazz and taking far too long solos and a leader that didn’t want to lead. But it was just the respect, it was…
